subject: Benchmark playbook & hands-on session — schedule confirmation and agenda
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme-ai.com>, Carla Ruiz <carla.ruiz@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Planning: hands-on benchmark session for Acme POC

Hi Alex / Carla —

Following up from our discovery call — thanks again for the context. Wed like to lock a 2.5 hour hands-on session to validate performance and the end-to-end runbook. Primary goals:
- Walk through prompt sets and routing policy that Acme plans to use
- Run a short suite of load tests (warmup + 3 steady-state profiles) to validate throughput and latency SLOs
- Review the test harness and artifact collection (traces, token-level costs, p95/p99)

Proposed windows (PT):
- Tue Nov 30, 10:00–12:30
- Wed Dec 1, 13:00–15:30
- Thu Dec 2, 08:30–11:00

Targets well try to validate in-session (tentative):
- Throughput: sustained 250 concurrent requests / ~1.2k tokens/sec overall (across pooled workers)
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms, p99 < 700ms for the primary prompt set

Pre-reqs from your side: shared prompt set (sample_prompts.csv), any routing rules that will be used in production, and a contact who can approve model variant pinning during the session. Ive attached an initial runbook and a sample load config.

If those windows don't work, tell me two alternatives and well adjust. Once we pick a slot Ill circulate a short agenda and a link to the test harness repo.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks Rachel — appreciate the clear goals. Wed Dec 1 looks best for us but were in Eastern Time (ET); would that be 16:00–18:30 ET? Also, a quick ask: can we shift the session later in the week if our legal team needs to review data handling notes? If needed we could do Fri Dec 3 instead.

Quick confirmations:
- We can provide the prompt set and routing rules by Monday Nov 29.
- Our target for production would be closer to 300 reqs concurrent (we want to push a bit higher), but were comfortable starting with your proposed targets in-session and running a follow-up spike if we need more headroom.

Could you also confirm the load generator youll run (k6 vs. Locust vs. internal harness) and whether youll need any ephemeral VPC access?

Alex / Rachel — looping in Marissa from Solutions so we have coverage on the runbook and post-session follow-up. A couple of practical notes from the engagement team before we lock: 

1) Test harness / generator: we usually run the PoC with our Git-backed harness (link below) that can produce both steady-state RPS and mixed user scenarios. We can also export k6 scripts if you prefer. For this session we recommend starting with the Redwood harness and an export you can run later.

2) Agenda (proposed 2.5 hr):
   - 0:00–0:20 Introduction & goals, model variant pinning
   - 0:20–0:50 Prompt review + prompt-level latency checks (sample_prompts.csv)
   - 0:50–1:30 Warmup + KV cache priming + baseline steady-state run (profile A)
   - 1:30–2:10 Peak load test with routing rules applied (profile B)
   - 2:10–2:30 Artifact collection & next steps (traces, token costs, p95/p99)

3) Data / access: we do not need customer data in-session. Please bring synthetic prompt sets or redacted samples. If we need VPC peering for higher fidelity tests we can discuss offline; it isnt required for the first run.

4) Acceptance criteria for the session: well capture whether throughput meets expected range (+/- 15%), and whether latency SLOs hold during the peak profile. If we miss, we document mitigation (batching configs, quantization suggestion, routing split).

Ill attach a short checklist in the runbook; Rachel, can you share the drive link and the harness repo in the final confirmation?

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: none (runbook link to follow)
